record.original_question: Fix positive integers k and n with k < n. Define a decreasing sequence by n0 = n and n_{i+1} = max{p : p <= n_i - k and p is prime}. Determine the length of this sequence, that is, the number of terms before it terminates.

evidence.quote: Let k, n 0 N*, k < n. We define a decreasing sequence of integers: no = n and ni+1 = max {p, p... - k, p is a prime}, for i > 0. Find the length (the number of terms) of this sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let k and n be positive integers with k < n. Define a finite decreasing sequence of nonnegative integers (n_i) recursively as follows. Set n_0 = n. Given n_i, if there exists a prime p with p ≤ n_i - k, set n_{i+1} = max{ p : p is prime and p ≤ n_i - k }; otherwise, terminate the sequence at n_i. Determine, as a function of k and n, the length of this sequence (i.e., the number of terms it contains before termination).
artifact.status_search_result: No specific source was found that gives a closed-form or asymptotic answer to the length of this prime-step decreasing sequence as a function of k and n. The question depends on the irregular distribution of prime gaps, so its exact behavior appears not to be settled in the literature.
